name: Design Library
description: Machine-readable component and template catalog for Habibi/Nexus-style product surfaces.

entries.name: Button
entries.description: Buttons trigger important actions across Design Library surfaces. They use Habibi action tokens, explicit variants, stable sizing, visible focus states, and clear leading, trailing, loading, and icon-only slots.

props.name: variant
props.description: Controls the visual treatment and semantic emphasis.

props.name: size
props.description: Controls height, padding, and text size.

props.name: leadingIcon
props.description: Optional icon rendered before the label.

props.name: trailingIcon
props.description: Optional icon rendered after the label.

props.name: loading
props.description: Disables the button and replaces the leading slot with a spinner.

useWhen: Use primary buttons for the single most important action in a region.
Use secondary buttons for supporting actions near a primary action.
Use tertiary buttons for low-emphasis inline actions.
Use destructive buttons only for actions that remove, delete, revoke, or reset.
Use icon-only buttons for compact toolbars when the icon is widely understood and an accessible label is provided.
doNotUseWhen: Do not place multiple primary buttons in the same action group.
Do not use a destructive button for reversible navigation.
Do not rely on icon-only buttons without an accessible label.
Do not use loading buttons without preserving enough width for the action label.
accessibility: Buttons use semantic button elements.
Focus states are visible through the Habibi focus ring.
Loading and disabled states prevent repeated submission.
Icon-only buttons require an aria-label.
Button labels should describe the action, not the destination or generic confirmation.
agentGuidance: Choose one primary button per screen or modal footer.
Pair primary and secondary actions in predictable order: secondary left, primary right.
Prefer action-specific labels like 'Create Agent' or 'Save Changes' instead of generic labels like 'Submit'.
If generating an icon-only action, include aria-label and choose size='icon'.

entries.name: Chat Surface
entries.description: Chat Surface frames an agent conversation with header, scrollable stream, suggestions, and composer.
useWhen: Use as the parent container for agent conversations.
Compose with Chat Message, Suggestion Chips, and Composer.
doNotUseWhen: Do not use Chat Surface for static documentation.
Do not place unrelated dashboard panels inside the message stream.
accessibility: Conversation regions should preserve reading order.
Composer remains reachable after the message stream.
agentGuidance: Use Chat Surface for any interactive agent workspace.
Keep system chrome outside the message stream.
entries.code:
import { ChatSurface } from "./ChatSurface";

<ChatSurface>
  <ChatMessage role="user">Show campaign performance.</ChatMessage>
  <Composer />
</ChatSurface>

entries.name: Chat Message
entries.description: Chat Message renders user, agent, and system turns with avatar, timestamp, content, and optional actions.

props.name: actions
props.description: Shows copy and feedback action buttons.

useWhen: Use for every turn in a conversation.
Use system messages for tool events or state changes.
Use actions on agent responses.
doNotUseWhen: Do not hide important system events outside the stream.
Do not use message bubbles for non-conversation cards.
accessibility: Messages preserve semantic reading order.
Action buttons should have accessible labels in production.
agentGuidance: Use role='user' for user-authored turns and role='agent' for assistant responses.
Use system messages for tool or workflow state.
entries.code:
import { ChatMessage } from "./ChatMessage";

<ChatMessage role="agent" actions>
  The evaluation completed successfully.
</ChatMessage>

entries.name: Composer / Chat Input
entries.description: Composer captures chat input with attachment, microphone, send action, helper text, and character count.
useWhen: Use at the bottom of agent chat surfaces.
Use helper text to explain keyboard behavior.
Keep send disabled until content exists in production.
doNotUseWhen: Do not make the composer scroll away in primary chat experiences.
Do not omit labels for icon-only actions.
accessibility: Textarea is keyboard accessible.
Icon-only controls include aria labels.
agentGuidance: Use Composer for agent chat and prompt entry.
Use Textarea for settings forms and Composer for conversational input.

entries.name: Suggestion Chips
entries.description: Suggestion Chips offer fast follow-up prompts and next actions after agent responses.
useWhen: Use after agent responses to reduce typing effort.
Use for common follow-up actions and prompt starters.
doNotUseWhen: Do not show too many chips at once.
Do not use vague suggestions like 'More'.
accessibility: Chips are buttons and keyboard reachable.
Labels describe the action directly.
agentGuidance: Generate chips that continue the user's current task.
Keep chip labels short and action-oriented.
entries.code:
import { SuggestionChips } from "./SuggestionChips";

<SuggestionChips suggestions={["Show sources", "Export summary"]} />

entries.name: Thinking / Streaming State
entries.description: Streaming State shows what the agent is doing while a response or tool call is in progress.
useWhen: Use when an agent response is streaming or a tool call is active.
Name the current activity when possible.
doNotUseWhen: Do not show anonymous loading for long AI actions.
Do not use only animated dots without text.
accessibility: Visible text describes the activity.
Future implementation should respect reduced motion preferences.
agentGuidance: Use activity-specific labels like 'Calling analytics tool' rather than generic 'Loading'.
Pair streaming state with the message that will receive output.
entries.code:
import { StreamingState } from "./StreamingState";

<StreamingState label="Calling analytics tool" />

entries.name: Citation Chip
entries.description: Citation Chip links an agent claim to a specific source, excerpt, or evidence item.

props.name: index
props.description: Numeric citation marker that maps to the source drawer.

props.name: source
props.description: Optional source family or system label.

useWhen: Use next to agent claims that need evidence.
Use numbered citations when a Source Drawer is present.
Use confidence only when it comes from a real scoring model.
doNotUseWhen: Do not use citations as decorative tags.
Do not show confidence values that are not backed by data.
accessibility: Citation chips are buttons and reachable by keyboard.
The label should identify the source action without relying on the number alone.
agentGuidance: Use Citation Chip whenever an answer references source material.
Pair indexed chips with Source Drawer entries using the same index.
entries.code:
import { CitationChip } from "./CitationChip";

<CitationChip index={1} label="Regional lift summary" source="Analytics run" tone="brand" />

entries.name: Tool Call Card
entries.description: Tool Call Card exposes an agent's connected tool activity, including running, complete, and review states.

props.name: description
props.description: Short explanation of what the tool is doing.

props.name: meta
props.description: Optional endpoint, run id, or internal tool identifier.

useWhen: Use when a tool call should be visible to users.
Use inside chat streams, activity feeds, or run detail panels.
doNotUseWhen: Do not expose sensitive internal payloads.
Do not use for normal static status badges.
accessibility: Status is visible as text, not color alone.
Long tool details should remain in reading order.
agentGuidance: Use Tool Call Card for transparent agent actions like retrieval, analysis, export, or validation.
Summarize payloads instead of rendering raw JSON by default.
entries.code:
import { ToolCallCard } from "./ToolCallCard";

<ToolCallCard status="running" toolName="Analytics Query">
  Fetching campaign metrics by region.
</ToolCallCard>

entries.name: Source Drawer
entries.description: Source Drawer collects the sources behind an agent answer so users can inspect evidence without leaving the workflow.

props.name: sources
props.description: Source rows with id, title, meta, and excerpt.

useWhen: Use beside agent responses that contain citations.
Use for source review, audit, and evidence inspection.
doNotUseWhen: Do not put primary navigation in Source Drawer.
Do not hide critical evidence behind unlabeled icons.
accessibility: Sources are rendered as articles in a readable sequence.
Future drawer behavior should include focus management when opened as an overlay.
agentGuidance: Use Source Drawer as the destination for Citation Chip source inspection.
Keep excerpts concise and include enough metadata to judge trust.

entries.name: Agent Avatar
entries.description: Agent Avatar represents an agent, user, or system identity with size, tone, and status variants.
useWhen: Use in chat messages, agent headers, run cards, and identity rows.
Use status when the agent is actively working or complete.
doNotUseWhen: Do not use decorative avatars without identity meaning.
Do not rely on the status dot without nearby status text for critical states.
accessibility: Avatar exposes an image role with an accessible label.
Status dot exposes a short status label.
agentGuidance: Use Agent Avatar for AI or system identities instead of generic Avatar when the status matters.
Use the user tone for human-authored turns.

entries.name: Thinking State
entries.description: Thinking State shows a compact step list for what an agent is doing while work is in progress.
useWhen: Use for multi-step agent work that takes more than a moment.
Use when naming the work increases trust and reduces perceived wait time.
doNotUseWhen: Do not expose private chain-of-thought.
Do not use for instant loading states where Spinner or Streaming State is enough.
accessibility: Steps are rendered as an ordered list.
Active work includes text as well as animation.
agentGuidance: Use Thinking State for transparent process summaries, not hidden reasoning.
Describe observable workflow steps like retrieval, validation, or drafting.
entries.code:
import { ThinkingState } from "./ThinkingState";

<ThinkingState label="Checking sources" steps={steps} />

entries.name: Agent Manifest
entries.description: Agent Manifest exposes the component and template catalog as predictable JSON for AI tools and code-generation agents.
useWhen: Load the manifest before generating Design Library UI.
Select entries by category, component kind, props, variants, tokens, and agent guidance.
doNotUseWhen: Do not scrape visual docs when the manifest is available.
Do not generate components that are not present in the manifest unless they are approved gaps.
accessibility: The manifest entry provides visible endpoint text and readable summary metrics.
Generated UI should still follow each entry's accessibility notes.
agentGuidance: Fetch the manifest, choose from approved entries, and honor useWhen, doNotUseWhen, props, variants, and tokens.
For templates, copy composition patterns before inventing new layouts.

entries.name: Chart Container
entries.description: Chart Container wraps chart visuals with title, description, toolbar, border, radius, and spacing.
useWhen: Use around every dashboard chart.
Use description to clarify timeframe or measurement.
doNotUseWhen: Do not place charts in unlabelled containers.
Do not omit empty/loading/error states in production wrappers.
accessibility: Chart title gives the visualization a text anchor.
Future wrappers should expose data tables or summaries for screen readers.
agentGuidance: Use Chart Container before placing any chart in dashboards.
Add a toolbar only when it changes the chart data.

entries.name: Chart Legend
entries.description: Legend maps chart colors to human-readable series labels.
useWhen: Use when a chart has multiple series or non-obvious colors.
Keep labels short and specific.
doNotUseWhen: Do not rely on legend color alone when labels can be direct.
Do not use vague labels like Series 1.
accessibility: Legend text names each series.
Colors should not be the only differentiator in complex charts.
agentGuidance: Use legend for multi-series dashboards.
For one-series charts, title and axis labels may be enough.
entries.code:
import { ChartLegend } from "./ChartLegend";

<ChartLegend items={[{ color: "#6941C6", label: "Current period" }]} />

entries.name: Chart Tooltip
entries.description: Chart Tooltip shows the active point, category, and value during hover or focus.
useWhen: Use for precise chart values.
Format values for the domain.
doNotUseWhen: Do not require hover to understand the chart.
Do not show raw unformatted data.
accessibility: Tooltips should have keyboard/focus equivalents in production chart wrappers.
agentGuidance: Use Chart Tooltip for hoverable data points and bars.
Keep values formatted and concise.
entries.code:
import { ChartTooltip } from "./ChartTooltip";

<ChartTooltip label="April 2026" value="148 conversations" />

entries.name: Line Chart
entries.description: Line Chart shows trend over time with points and a tokenized brand stroke.
useWhen: Use for time-series trends.
Use points when individual observations matter.
doNotUseWhen: Do not use line charts for unrelated categories.
Do not overload with too many series.
accessibility: SVG has an image role and label in this first implementation.
Production charts should expose data summaries.
agentGuidance: Use Line Chart for quality, latency, cost, and volume trends over time.

entries.name: Area Chart
entries.description: Area Chart emphasizes volume or magnitude over time with a subtle filled region.
useWhen: Use for volume trends and cumulative-feeling metrics.
Keep fill opacity low so the chart stays quiet.
doNotUseWhen: Do not use area fill when exact comparison matters more than trend shape.
accessibility: SVG has an image role and label in this first implementation.
agentGuidance: Use Area Chart for conversation volume, degradation, or response quality over time.

entries.name: Bar Chart
entries.description: Bar Chart compares values across categories or time buckets.
useWhen: Use for comparisons across categories.
Highlight the selected or latest bar when useful.
doNotUseWhen: Do not use bars for continuous relationships better shown as lines.
accessibility: SVG has an image role and label in this first implementation.
agentGuidance: Use Bar Chart for workspace counts, monthly usage, and ranked comparisons.

entries.name: Donut Chart
entries.description: Donut Chart shows part-to-whole progress or distribution with a center value.
useWhen: Use for small part-to-whole summaries.
Use center text for the main value.
doNotUseWhen: Do not use donut charts for precise comparison across many categories.
Do not use more than 4-6 segments.
accessibility: SVG has an image role and label in this first implementation.
agentGuidance: Use Donut Chart for completion, distribution, and simple category shares.

entries.name: Summary Chart Card
entries.description: Summary Chart Card combines a KPI, trend badge, and compact chart preview.
useWhen: Use in dashboard overview grids.
Pair the value with a trend and compact chart.
doNotUseWhen: Do not use for detailed analysis; link to a full chart view.
Do not omit the metric label.
accessibility: Value and label are visible text.
Compact chart should be supplemental.
agentGuidance: Use Summary Chart Card for dashboard overviews and generated analytics sections.

entries.name: Dashboard Header
entries.description: Dashboard Header introduces a product workspace with title, description, status, and primary actions.

props.name: eyebrow
props.description: Small context label above the title.

useWhen: Use at the top of dashboard, workspace, and run-detail pages.
Place primary page actions in the action slot.
doNotUseWhen: Do not use for card-level headings.
Do not overload the header with every available action.
accessibility: Uses a semantic header and h1 title.
Action controls preserve visible labels.
agentGuidance: Use Dashboard Header once per full-page dashboard or workspace view.
Pair it with Workspace Switcher when the user can change context.

entries.name: Workspace Switcher
entries.description: Workspace Switcher lets users move between product, agent, or dashboard contexts.

props.name: workspaces
props.description: Workspace options with label, meta, and selected state.

useWhen: Use when a user can switch between Nexus, marketing, INCI, or other project spaces.
Keep metadata short so the selected workspace scans quickly.
doNotUseWhen: Do not use for local tabs inside one panel.
Do not mix workspace selection with destructive actions.
accessibility: Items are buttons with visible labels.
Production dropdown behavior should add menu semantics and keyboard roving focus.
agentGuidance: Use Workspace Switcher near the top of cross-project surfaces.
Prefer Tabs for local page sections and Workspace Switcher for global context.

entries.name: Run Status Pill
entries.description: Run Status Pill communicates the state of an agent run, export, analysis, or queued job.
useWhen: Use in dashboard headers, tables, activity rows, and run cards.
Use visible text with color so status is not color-only.
doNotUseWhen: Do not use for arbitrary tags.
Do not show running animation for inactive states.
accessibility: Status is shown as text and icon.
Running icon is decorative because the label carries the meaning.
agentGuidance: Use Run Status Pill for job-like states only.
Use Badge for simpler labels that are not workflow state.

entries.name: Activity Feed
entries.description: Activity Feed shows recent agent actions, workspace events, and system updates in a dashboard context.

props.name: items
props.description: Feed rows with label, description, meta, type, and status.

useWhen: Use on dashboards that need recent work visibility.
Use for audit-friendly product events and agent activity.
doNotUseWhen: Do not use for long-form logs where a table or timeline is better.
Do not mix unrelated product areas without context.
accessibility: Feed is an ordered list with readable event text.
Status text is visible in each row.
agentGuidance: Use Activity Feed when summarizing what happened recently.
Use Timeline when event sequence and dates are the primary content.

entries.name: Insight Card
entries.description: Insight Card highlights an agent-generated recommendation, risk, or opportunity with a clear next action.
useWhen: Use for one high-signal recommendation or risk.
Pair with charts, tables, or source drawers when evidence is available.
doNotUseWhen: Do not use for generic marketing copy.
Do not stack too many insight cards without prioritization.
accessibility: Insight title and description are readable without the icon.
The review action has visible text.
agentGuidance: Use Insight Card for synthesized recommendations, not raw facts.
Keep each card to one decision or action.
entries.code:
import { InsightCard } from "./InsightCard";

<InsightCard title="Performance is improving" description="Response quality increased by region." metric="+4.2%" />

entries.name: Quick Action Panel
entries.description: Quick Action Panel combines search with common product actions so users can move quickly in a workspace.

props.name: actions
props.description: Action rows with label, description, and type.

useWhen: Use on dashboard home pages and workspaces where repeated actions matter.
Keep actions specific and task-oriented.
doNotUseWhen: Do not use as a replacement for full navigation.
Do not include actions that require dangerous confirmation without a confirm step.
accessibility: Search input has an accessible label.
Actions are buttons with visible labels and descriptions.
agentGuidance: Use Quick Action Panel to expose common AI workflows such as chat, analysis, source review, and drafting.
Keep labels short and descriptions concrete.

entries.name: Table
entries.description: Table presents structured rows and columns for dashboards, feedback, agents, runs, and evaluation data.

props.name: columns
props.description: Column definitions and optional cell renderers.

useWhen: Use for comparable structured records.
Use badge cells for status.
Pair with filters and pagination for large datasets.
doNotUseWhen: Do not use tables for narrative content.
Do not make users scan large tables without search or filters.
accessibility: Uses semantic table, thead, th, tbody, and td elements.
Header cells use scope.
agentGuidance: Use Table for agent lists, feedback, runs, and evaluation data.
Use Empty State when there are no rows.

entries.name: List
entries.description: List presents compact stacked items with optional leading icons, metadata, and descriptions.

props.name: items
props.description: List items with title, optional description, leading slot, and meta slot.

useWhen: Use for recent activity, agents, sources, and short collections.
Use meta for time, status, or counts.
doNotUseWhen: Do not use lists for dense comparison; use Table.
Do not overload list rows with too many actions.
accessibility: Use semantic list structure in future enhancements where needed.
Keep row labels readable and descriptive.
agentGuidance: Use List for compact activity and source collections.
Use Table when users compare multiple fields.
entries.code:
import { List } from "./List";

<List items={[{ title: "Analytics Agent", description: "Ready" }]} />

entries.name: Description List
entries.description: Description List presents labeled metadata for detail panels, modals, and drawers.
useWhen: Use in detail panels, feedback modals, and source drawers.
Use for stable metadata that users scan by label.
doNotUseWhen: Do not use for editable forms.
Do not use for large row sets.
accessibility: Uses semantic dl, dt, and dd elements.
Labels and values remain paired.
agentGuidance: Use Description List for source metadata, agent settings summaries, and modal details.
entries.code:
import { DescriptionList } from "./DescriptionList";

<DescriptionList items={[{ label: "Status", value: "Active" }]} />

entries.name: Stat / KPI Card
entries.description: Stat cards highlight key metrics with optional trend, helper text, and icon slot.
useWhen: Use for dashboard summaries.
Include trend or helper context when possible.
Use a grid for related metrics.
doNotUseWhen: Do not show numbers without context.
Do not use too many stat cards above the fold.
accessibility: Use clear labels and values.
Do not rely on trend color alone.
agentGuidance: Use Stat Card for KPI overviews and analytics dashboards.
Add helper text that answers 'so what?'.
entries.code:
import { StatCard } from "./StatCard";

<StatCard label="Conversations" value="148" trend="+12%" />

entries.name: Empty State
entries.description: Empty State explains what would appear in an empty region and gives the user a clear next action.

props.name: description
props.description: Explains what happened and what to do next.

useWhen: Use whenever a list, table, or page has no content.
Give users a recovery or creation action.
doNotUseWhen: Do not show blank panels.
Do not use vague text like 'No data' without guidance.
accessibility: Uses readable text and a real action button when provided.
Icon is decorative unless paired with text.
agentGuidance: Use Empty State for first-use, no-results, and no-data cases.
Always explain the next useful action.
entries.code:
import { EmptyState } from "./EmptyState";

<EmptyState title="No agents yet" description="Create an agent to get started." actionLabel="Create first agent" />

entries.name: Timeline
entries.description: Timeline presents ordered events such as agent turns, tool calls, runs, and audit activity.
useWhen: Use for chronological activity.
Use badges for event types and statuses.
doNotUseWhen: Do not use timeline for unordered lists.
Do not hide timestamps when sequence matters.
accessibility: Uses ordered list semantics.
Event text includes meaning beyond color.
agentGuidance: Use Timeline for eval replay, tool-call history, and activity feeds.
entries.code:
import { Timeline } from "./Timeline";

<Timeline items={[{ title: "Turn 1", time: "10:24 AM", content: "User query received." }]} />

entries.name: Accordion
entries.description: Accordion reveals and hides grouped content such as help text, FAQs, and progressive detail.

props.name: items
props.description: Disclosure rows with title, content, and defaultOpen state.

useWhen: Use for secondary detail that should not dominate the page.
Use for FAQs, help text, and grouped configuration notes.
doNotUseWhen: Do not hide required form instructions inside an accordion.
Do not use for primary navigation.
accessibility: Uses native details and summary semantics.
Summary rows are keyboard reachable.
agentGuidance: Use Accordion for optional explanatory content.
Use Tabs for peer views and Tree for hierarchical navigation.

entries.name: Tree
entries.description: Tree displays nested workspaces, source libraries, folders, and agent/project hierarchies.

props.name: nodes
props.description: Nested nodes with label, children, metadata, and selected state.

useWhen: Use for source libraries, workspace folders, and nested project structures.
Use metadata for counts or short state labels.
doNotUseWhen: Do not use Tree for flat lists.
Do not create deep hierarchies without search.
accessibility: Preview uses navigation and list structure.
Production tree behavior should add full tree keyboard semantics when interactive.
agentGuidance: Use Tree when hierarchy matters to the task.
Use List for flat collections and Sidebar for primary routes.

entries.name: Data Toolbar
entries.description: Data Toolbar combines search, filters, selected filter tags, result count, refresh, and export actions for data views.

props.name: resultCount
props.description: Visible result count or data summary.

useWhen: Use above tables, source lists, and run lists.
Use active tags to make filters visible and removable.
doNotUseWhen: Do not add toolbar controls that do not affect the data below.
Do not hide active filters only inside a menu.
accessibility: Search input has an accessible label.
Icon actions use accessible labels through Icon Button.
agentGuidance: Use Data Toolbar with Table, List, and Pagination.
Use Quick Action Panel for task launch rather than data filtering.

entries.name: Form Field
entries.description: Form Field composes label, optional marker, control, helper text, and validation message into a consistent input unit.

props.name: optional
props.description: Marks optional fields. Required is the default.

useWhen: Use Form Field for every labeled form control.
Show helper text before users make errors.
Use error text with recovery instructions.
doNotUseWhen: Do not use placeholder text as the only label.
Do not mark every required field with an asterisk; mark optional fields instead.
accessibility: Labels are linked to controls with htmlFor.
Errors should be announced by connecting aria-describedby in future enhancements.
agentGuidance: Always compose Input, Select, Textarea, and Slider with Form Field when a visible label is needed.
Prefer explicit labels and helper text over vague placeholders.

entries.name: Input
entries.description: Input captures short text values such as names, emails, IDs, and filter terms.

props.name: disabled
props.description: Prevents input and applies disabled styling.

props.name: placeholder
props.description: Format hint, not a replacement for label.

useWhen: Use for short free-text values.
Use placeholder text to show format examples.
Pair with Form Field for labels and helper text.
doNotUseWhen: Do not use for long-form prompts; use Textarea.
Do not hide labels inside placeholders.
accessibility: Uses native input semantics.
Invalid state sets aria-invalid.
agentGuidance: Use Input for one-line values only.
Use specific placeholders like you@unilever.com instead of 'Enter email'.

entries.name: Textarea
entries.description: Textarea captures longer free-form content such as prompts, descriptions, comments, and instructions.
useWhen: Use for multi-line input.
Use for system prompts and agent descriptions.
Pair with helper text for constraints.
doNotUseWhen: Do not use for single short values.
Do not validate on every keystroke.
accessibility: Uses native textarea semantics.
Invalid state sets aria-invalid.
agentGuidance: Use Textarea for prompts and explanations.
Keep helper text visible when content has rules or limits.
entries.code:
import { Textarea } from "./Textarea";

<Textarea placeholder="Describe the agent behavior" />

entries.name: Select
entries.description: Select lets users choose one option from a known set.
useWhen: Use when options are known and limited.
Use Combobox later for searchable or large option sets.
doNotUseWhen: Do not use Select for free-form values.
Do not include too many options without search.
accessibility: Uses native select semantics.
Visible label should come from Form Field.
agentGuidance: Use Select for compact controlled choices.
Use Combobox for user, project, or source lists once available.
entries.code:
import { Select } from "./Select";

<Select defaultValue="chat">
  <option value="chat">Chat app</option>
  <option value="dashboard">Dashboard</option>
</Select>

entries.name: Checkbox
entries.description: Checkbox captures independent yes/no choices, often with a descriptive label.
useWhen: Use for independent binary choices.
Use descriptions when the label alone is not enough.
doNotUseWhen: Do not use for mutually exclusive choices; use Radio or Select.
Do not create color-only checked states.
accessibility: Uses native checkbox input.
Label wraps the control for a larger click target.
agentGuidance: Use Checkbox for permission toggles and multi-select settings.
Use Switch for immediate on/off settings.
entries.code:
import { Checkbox } from "./Checkbox";

<Checkbox label="Use knowledge base" description="Allow approved document retrieval." />

entries.name: Switch
entries.description: Switch toggles an immediate on/off setting.
useWhen: Use for settings that can be toggled on or off.
Use when the change can be understood immediately.
doNotUseWhen: Do not use for submitting a form.
Do not use when choosing among more than two options.
accessibility: Uses native checkbox behavior visually styled as a switch.
Label expands the click target.
agentGuidance: Use Switch for feature enablement and policy toggles.
Use Checkbox when the choice is part of a form submission.
entries.code:
import { Switch } from "./Switch";

<Switch label="Enable live tool calls" />

entries.name: Slider
entries.description: Slider adjusts bounded numeric values such as temperature, depth, thresholds, and weighting.
useWhen: Use for bounded numeric tuning.
Pair with visible values when precision matters.
doNotUseWhen: Do not use when users need exact numeric entry only.
Do not hide the meaning of min/max.
accessibility: Uses native range input.
Provide a label for screen reader context.
agentGuidance: Use Slider for model parameters like temperature.
Add visible current value in templates where precision matters.
entries.code:
import { Slider } from "./Slider";

<Slider label="Temperature" min={0} max={100} defaultValue={35} />

entries.name: Search Input
entries.description: Search Input lets users filter catalog entries, tables, agents, templates, and dashboards.
useWhen: Use when a list has more than 20 items.
Use in topbars, filter bars, and catalog search.
doNotUseWhen: Do not add search to tiny lists.
Do not return blank empty states; provide helpful recovery copy.
accessibility: Uses native search input.
Provide a visible or sr-only label.
agentGuidance: Use Search Input for filtering existing content.
Use Command Palette for action search once available.
entries.code:
import { SearchInput } from "./SearchInput";

<SearchInput placeholder="Search agents, templates, or components" />

entries.name: Radio Group
entries.description: Radio Group captures one choice from a small set of mutually exclusive options.

props.name: options
props.description: Options with label, value, description, and disabled state.

useWhen: Use when users must choose exactly one option from a small set.
Use descriptions when the options have meaningful tradeoffs.
doNotUseWhen: Do not use for large option lists; use Select or Combobox.
Do not use Checkbox for mutually exclusive choices.
accessibility: Uses fieldset and native radio inputs.
Labels wrap each option for a larger click target.
agentGuidance: Use Radio Group for 2-5 mutually exclusive choices.
Use Select for compact static choices and Combobox for searchable lists.

entries.name: Segmented Control
entries.description: Segmented Control switches between compact peer modes or views within the same context.

props.name: segments
props.description: Segment labels, values, and active state.

useWhen: Use for small view or mode switches.
Use when all options should remain visible.
doNotUseWhen: Do not use for global navigation.
Do not use for long labels or many options.
accessibility: Segments expose pressed state.
A screen-reader label describes the control.
agentGuidance: Use Segmented Control for local modes like Components/Templates or Overview/Runs/Sources.
Use Tabs when the view change needs stronger page structure.

entries.name: Alert
entries.description: Alerts communicate contextual success, warning, error, or information inside the current page or section.
useWhen: Use for inline state messages close to the affected content.
Use error alerts with recovery instructions.
Use warning alerts before risky or delayed actions.
doNotUseWhen: Do not use alerts for global announcements; use Banner.
Do not show success without naming what happened.
accessibility: Error alerts use alert role.
Non-error alerts use status role.
Dismiss controls include accessible labels.
agentGuidance: Use Alert when the message belongs to a specific form, table, card, or section.
Include what happened and what the user can do next.
entries.code:
import { Alert } from "./Alert";

<Alert title="Could not save" variant="error">
  The agent name is empty. Add a name and try again.
</Alert>

entries.name: Banner
entries.description: Banners communicate page-level announcements, operational status, and persistent calls to action.
useWhen: Use for page-level or dashboard-level announcements.
Use actions when the banner asks the user to resolve something.
doNotUseWhen: Do not use banners for field validation.
Do not stack many banners at the top of a page.
accessibility: Uses alert role for error variant and status role for other variants.
Action and dismiss controls are keyboard reachable.
agentGuidance: Use Banner above the main content area for persistent operational context.
Prefer Alert for section-specific feedback.
entries.code:
import { Banner } from "./Banner";

<Banner title="Deployment review" action={<button>Review</button>}>
  This workspace has 3 agents waiting for approval.
</Banner>

entries.name: Spinner
entries.description: Spinner indicates short indeterminate loading states.
useWhen: Use for short loading states under a few seconds.
Pair with text when the wait has meaning.
doNotUseWhen: Do not use only a spinner for long operations; use Progress or Skeleton.
Do not leave users without context for slow operations.
accessibility: Uses status role.
Provides visible or screen-reader loading text.
agentGuidance: Use Spinner for brief async actions.
For page loads, prefer Skeleton so layout feels stable.

entries.name: Progress
entries.description: Progress shows determinate completion for imports, evaluations, deployments, and long-running tasks.
useWhen: Use when completion percentage is known.
Use for imports, deploys, replays, and checklists.
doNotUseWhen: Do not fake precision if the system cannot estimate progress.
Do not use for instant actions.
accessibility: Uses progressbar role and aria value attributes.
Visible label provides task context.
agentGuidance: Use Progress for long-running known tasks.
Use Spinner when progress cannot be estimated.
entries.code:
import { Progress } from "./Progress";

<Progress label="Knowledge import" value={68} />

entries.name: Skeleton
entries.description: Skeleton preserves layout while content loads, reducing perceived wait time and layout shift.
useWhen: Use for page, card, table, and chat loading states.
Match skeleton shape to the final content layout.
doNotUseWhen: Do not use skeletons for actions that complete almost instantly.
Do not show unrelated placeholder shapes.
accessibility: Skeletons are aria-hidden because they are visual placeholders.
Pair with a higher-level loading announcement when needed.
agentGuidance: Use Skeleton when content structure is known but data is not ready.
Use it in tables, cards, dashboards, and message streams.

entries.name: Modal / Dialog
entries.description: Modal interrupts the current workflow for focused confirmation, forms, or high-priority information.
useWhen: Use for blocking decisions or focused forms.
Use clear action labels in the footer.
Use destructive variants only for irreversible actions.
doNotUseWhen: Do not use modals for lightweight hints.
Do not stack modals.
Do not hide long workflows inside a small modal.
accessibility: Uses dialog semantics and aria-modal.
Close control has an accessible label.
Future Radix implementation should add focus trapping and Escape handling.
agentGuidance: Use Modal when the user must decide before continuing.
Use Drawer when context should remain visible.
entries.code:
import { Modal } from "./Modal";

<Modal open={open} onOpenChange={setOpen} title="Deploy agent">
  Review deployment details.
</Modal>

entries.name: Drawer
entries.description: Drawer exposes supporting details without fully removing the user from the current surface.
useWhen: Use for source details, trace panels, filters, and inspectors.
Use when users need to keep page context.
doNotUseWhen: Do not use drawers for small tooltips.
Do not use drawers when a full page is needed.
accessibility: Uses dialog semantics and aria-modal.
Close control has an accessible label.
Future Radix implementation should add focus trapping.
agentGuidance: Use Drawer for citations, source inspection, and dashboard detail panels.
Keep drawer content scannable and sectioned.
entries.code:
import { Drawer } from "./Drawer";

<Drawer open={open} onOpenChange={setOpen} title="Source details">
  Source metadata
</Drawer>

entries.name: Popover
entries.description: Popover shows anchored supporting content for compact explanations, quick settings, or lightweight panels.
useWhen: Use for lightweight contextual panels.
Use when content is more substantial than a tooltip.
doNotUseWhen: Do not use for destructive confirmations; use Popconfirm.
Do not put long workflows in popovers.
accessibility: Appears on hover and focus-within in this first implementation.
Future headless implementation should manage open state and focus.
agentGuidance: Use Popover for short settings, compact metadata, and contextual detail.
Use Tooltip for a sentence of help text.

entries.name: Popconfirm
entries.description: Popconfirm asks for lightweight confirmation near the action that triggered it.
useWhen: Use for quick confirmation of risky actions.
Keep the confirmation close to the triggering control.
doNotUseWhen: Do not use for irreversible high-impact actions that need full context.
Do not use generic labels like OK or Yes.
accessibility: Confirmation buttons are keyboard reachable.
Future headless implementation should manage focus and dismiss behavior.
agentGuidance: Use Popconfirm for table/list delete actions.
Use Modal when consequences need a longer explanation.
entries.code:
import { Popconfirm } from "./Popconfirm";

<Popconfirm title="Delete draft?" description="This cannot be undone.">
  <button>Delete</button>
</Popconfirm>

entries.name: Toast / Message
entries.description: Toast communicates short-lived feedback after an action, without blocking the workflow.
useWhen: Use after actions like save, copy, publish, or refresh.
Keep copy short and action-specific.
doNotUseWhen: Do not use toasts for information the user must act on later.
Do not show silent success when a toast is needed.
accessibility: Uses status role.
Loading variant includes spinner animation.
agentGuidance: Use Toast for short post-action confirmation.
Use Alert or Banner when feedback needs to remain visible.
entries.code:
import { Toast } from "./Toast";

<Toast title="Saved" variant="success">
  Your changes were saved.
</Toast>

entries.name: Form Section
entries.description: Form Section groups related fields under a heading, description, and body slot.
useWhen: Use to break long forms into readable field groups.
Use one section per meaningful setting area.
doNotUseWhen: Do not use for a single isolated field.
Do not nest form sections inside form sections.
accessibility: Renders as a section with a visible heading.
Keep fields inside the section in logical order.
agentGuidance: Use Form Section for settings, setup, and edit workflows.
Use Panel for non-form dashboard regions.

entries.name: Form Group
entries.description: Form Group lays out related fields in responsive one, two, or three-column grids.
useWhen: Use for fields that should scan together.
Use one column for long inputs and three columns for short comparable fields.
doNotUseWhen: Do not force three columns for complex controls.
Do not use arbitrary margins between fields when Form Group can own spacing.
accessibility: Preserves DOM reading order.
Labels remain owned by each child field.
agentGuidance: Use Form Group inside Form Section.
Prefer two columns for normal settings forms.

entries.name: Validation Message
entries.description: Validation Message provides field or form feedback with error, success, and info tones.
useWhen: Use below fields or near form actions when validation blocks progress.
Use success sparingly for confirmation that matters.
doNotUseWhen: Do not use color alone to communicate validation.
Do not show vague messages like 'Invalid input' without next steps.
accessibility: Message includes visible text and icon.
Production forms should connect messages with aria-describedby.
agentGuidance: Use Validation Message for form feedback only.
Use Alert for broader page-level feedback.
entries.code:
import { ValidationMessage } from "./ValidationMessage";

<ValidationMessage>Campaign name is required.</ValidationMessage>

entries.name: File Upload
entries.description: File Upload lets users attach source files, datasets, exports, or product documents.
useWhen: Use for CSV uploads, source documents, product files, and campaign assets.
State accepted formats and limits close to the control.
doNotUseWhen: Do not hide upload constraints until after failure.
Do not use for simple URL entry.
accessibility: Native file input remains present and keyboard reachable.
Upload area has visible label and description.
agentGuidance: Use File Upload when a workflow needs source material.
Pair with Validation Message for file type or size errors.
entries.code:
import { FileUpload } from "./FileUpload";

<FileUpload description="CSV or PDF up to 10 MB." />

entries.name: Combobox
entries.description: Combobox combines a selectable value with an option list for agent, workspace, or source selection.

props.name: placeholder
props.description: Fallback text when no value is selected.

useWhen: Use when users choose from known options and may eventually need search.
Use for agent, workspace, project, or source selection.
doNotUseWhen: Do not use Combobox for very small binary choices.
Do not use without keyboard support in production.
accessibility: This preview documents visual structure; production should use combobox ARIA and keyboard behavior.
Selected option has a visible check icon.
agentGuidance: Use Combobox when option lists may grow or need filtering.
Use Select for small static lists.

entries.name: Date Picker
entries.description: Date Picker captures a date value for runs, reports, campaign windows, and review deadlines.
useWhen: Use for date-specific filters, schedules, and deadlines.
Use clear date formatting aligned with the user locale.
doNotUseWhen: Do not use Date Picker for free-text time ranges.
Do not build calendar behavior from scratch in production.
accessibility: The preview is a button trigger with visible text.
Production calendar should support keyboard navigation and focus management.
agentGuidance: Use Date Picker for one date.
Use a date range component when selecting start and end dates together.

entries.name: Form Actions
entries.description: Form Actions places cancel, save, submit, or review controls at the end of a form.
useWhen: Use at the end of forms and settings sections.
Keep the primary action last in left-to-right layouts.
doNotUseWhen: Do not place unrelated navigation in Form Actions.
Do not repeat the same primary action in multiple places.
accessibility: Buttons keep visible labels.
Action order should match product risk and workflow expectations.
agentGuidance: Use Form Actions at the bottom of Form Section.
Use Button variants to separate primary and secondary intent.

entries.name: Color
entries.description: Color tokens define brand, neutral, semantic, and dark-mode roles for all components.
useWhen: Use brand tokens for primary actions, focus, links, and selected states.
Use semantic tokens for status and feedback.
Use gray tokens for structure, text, borders, and quiet surfaces.
doNotUseWhen: Do not hardcode raw values inside component code when a Habibi token exists.
Do not introduce one-off scales without adding them to the token layer.
accessibility: Foundation choices must preserve WCAG AA contrast for text and UI controls.
Use visible focus states for every interactive element.
Do not use color as the only signal for status or meaning.
agentGuidance: Prefer token names over hex values.
Use semantic tokens with text or icon labels so meaning is not color-only.

entries.name: Typography
entries.description: Typography defines readable, scannable text roles across dense internal tools and agent surfaces.
useWhen: Use 14px as the minimum body text size.
Use monospace for code, tool names, and machine-readable identifiers.
Keep line length between 45 and 75 characters for reading surfaces.
doNotUseWhen: Do not hardcode raw values inside component code when a Habibi token exists.
Do not introduce one-off scales without adding them to the token layer.
accessibility: Foundation choices must preserve WCAG AA contrast for text and UI controls.
Use visible focus states for every interactive element.
Do not use color as the only signal for status or meaning.
agentGuidance: Reserve display styles for page-level headings.
Use text-sm for compact controls and tables, but avoid body copy below 14px.

entries.name: Spacing
entries.description: Spacing uses a 4px-based scale so layouts, components, and templates compose predictably.
useWhen: Use small spacing tokens for icon gaps and compact controls.
Use medium spacing tokens for cards, forms, and sections.
Use large spacing tokens for major page separation.
doNotUseWhen: Do not hardcode raw values inside component code when a Habibi token exists.
Do not introduce one-off scales without adding them to the token layer.
accessibility: Foundation choices must preserve WCAG AA contrast for text and UI controls.
Use visible focus states for every interactive element.
Do not use color as the only signal for status or meaning.
agentGuidance: Choose spacing tokens by composition level: slot, component, section, page.
Do not create arbitrary pixel gaps in generated UI.

entries.name: Radius
entries.description: Radius tokens define the shape language for controls, cards, overlays, and pills.
useWhen: Use radius-md for buttons and inputs.
Use radius-lg for cards, modals, and chart containers.
Use radius-full for pills, dots, and circular avatars.
doNotUseWhen: Do not hardcode raw values inside component code when a Habibi token exists.
Do not introduce one-off scales without adding them to the token layer.
accessibility: Foundation choices must preserve WCAG AA contrast for text and UI controls.
Use visible focus states for every interactive element.
Do not use color as the only signal for status or meaning.
agentGuidance: Do not make every surface overly rounded.
Match radius to the component role, not personal taste.

entries.name: Shadows
entries.description: Shadow tokens communicate subtle elevation without making internal tools feel decorative.
useWhen: Use subtle shadows for controls and cards.
Use stronger shadows only for overlays and modals.
Prefer borders over shadows when elevation is not meaningful.
doNotUseWhen: Do not hardcode raw values inside component code when a Habibi token exists.
Do not introduce one-off scales without adding them to the token layer.
accessibility: Foundation choices must preserve WCAG AA contrast for text and UI controls.
Use visible focus states for every interactive element.
Do not use color as the only signal for status or meaning.
agentGuidance: Use elevation to clarify stacking and interaction.
Do not stack multiple heavy shadows on one surface.

entries.name: Dark Mode
entries.description: Dark mode maps surfaces, text, and borders deliberately instead of simply inverting colors.
useWhen: Use mapped dark surfaces for app backgrounds, cards, inputs, and overlays.
Keep semantic colors recognizable in both themes.
Use dark borders to separate surfaces without washing out the interface.
doNotUseWhen: Do not hardcode raw values inside component code when a Habibi token exists.
Do not introduce one-off scales without adding them to the token layer.
accessibility: Foundation choices must preserve WCAG AA contrast for text and UI controls.
Use visible focus states for every interactive element.
Do not use color as the only signal for status or meaning.
agentGuidance: When generating dark UI, swap surface roles rather than inverting light tokens.
Keep focus and status states visible against dark surfaces.

entries.name: Container
entries.description: Container sets responsive page width and horizontal gutters for full-page layouts.
useWhen: Use once around main page content.
Use size to control reading width and dashboard density.
doNotUseWhen: Do not nest containers inside containers.
Do not use Container for card padding.
accessibility: Container does not change semantics.
Pair with main, section, or header landmarks as needed.
agentGuidance: Use Container for page-level horizontal rhythm.
Use Panel or Card for framed content instead of Container.
entries.code:
import { Container } from "./Container";

<Container size="lg">
  <DashboardHeader title="Analytics workspace" />
</Container>

entries.name: Stack
entries.description: Stack arranges child elements in a consistent vertical or horizontal flow.
useWhen: Use for simple repeated spacing between sibling elements.
Use inside forms, panels, and dashboard regions.
doNotUseWhen: Do not use Stack when CSS grid semantics are clearer.
Do not use ad hoc margins between children when Stack can own spacing.
accessibility: Stack preserves child order.
Use semantic child elements inside the slot.
agentGuidance: Use Stack as the default composition primitive for vertical rhythm.
Use Grid when children should align into columns.

entries.name: Grid
entries.description: Grid arranges cards, metrics, and panels into responsive columns.
useWhen: Use for dashboards, card groups, and repeated tiles.
Use responsive columns instead of fixed pixel widths.
doNotUseWhen: Do not use for one-dimensional lists.
Do not force too many columns into narrow viewports.
accessibility: Grid does not change reading order.
Keep visual order aligned with DOM order.
agentGuidance: Use Grid for repeatable dashboard modules.
Use Stack for single-column flows.
entries.code:
import { Grid } from "./Grid";

<Grid columns={3}>
  <StatCard label="Quality" value="87.3%" />
</Grid>

entries.name: Card
entries.description: Card frames one repeatable object with optional title and footer slots.
useWhen: Use for repeatable objects like workspaces, sources, or insights.
Use footer for secondary actions.
doNotUseWhen: Do not put cards inside cards.
Do not use Card as a full page section.
accessibility: Card renders as an article.
The title slot provides a local heading when present.
agentGuidance: Use Card for one object; use Panel for a larger region with internal content.
Never nest Card inside Card.
entries.code:
import { Card } from "./Card";

<Card title="Workspace card">Card content</Card>

entries.name: Panel
entries.description: Panel frames a larger dashboard region with header, description, actions, and body slots.
useWhen: Use for dashboard regions, data tables, and grouped workflow content.
Use actions for region-level commands.
doNotUseWhen: Do not use Panel for a single small object where Card is enough.
Do not nest panels inside panels.
accessibility: Panel renders as a section.
Use clear titles for landmark-like regions.
agentGuidance: Use Panel for major dashboard blocks.
Use Card inside Grid for repeatable objects, not Panel.
entries.code:
import { Panel } from "./Panel";

<Panel title="Recent activity" actions={<Button>View all</Button>}>
  Content
</Panel>

entries.name: Section
entries.description: Section creates full-width page bands with optional intro copy and constrained inner content.
useWhen: Use to divide full-page experiences into bands.
Use when a section needs its own intro copy.
doNotUseWhen: Do not style sections as floating cards.
Do not use Section inside Card or Panel.
accessibility: Section renders as a section landmark.
Use headings in order across the page.
agentGuidance: Use Section for page bands and Container for page gutters.
Do not place Section inside framed surfaces.
entries.code:
import { Section } from "./Section";

<Section title="Dashboard section" tone="muted">
  <Grid columns={2}>...</Grid>
</Section>

entries.name: Sidebar
entries.description: Sidebar provides persistent workspace navigation with active item and metadata slots.

props.name: items
props.description: Navigation rows with label, meta, and active state.

useWhen: Use for persistent app or workspace navigation.
Use active state to show the current route.
doNotUseWhen: Do not use Sidebar for short local option lists.
Do not hide important labels behind icons only.
accessibility: Sidebar contains a labeled nav region.
Navigation items are keyboard reachable buttons in this demo.
agentGuidance: Use Sidebar in full-page app shells.
Use Tabs or Menu for local navigation inside a panel.

entries.name: Topbar
entries.description: Topbar provides workspace title, search, utility actions, and user identity in an application shell.
useWhen: Use at the top of app shells and workspaces.
Use search only when the workspace supports search.
doNotUseWhen: Do not use Topbar inside a card.
Do not duplicate page-level actions already in Dashboard Header.
accessibility: Icon controls include aria labels.
Search input has an accessible label.
agentGuidance: Use Topbar with Sidebar for full application shell templates.
Use Dashboard Header for page content title below the shell.

entries.name: Tabs
entries.description: Tabs switch between peer sections within the same page, panel, or workspace.

props.name: items
props.description: Tab labels with optional count and active state.

useWhen: Use for sibling views at the same hierarchy level.
Use counts for lists, runs, or source totals.
doNotUseWhen: Do not use tabs for global navigation.
Do not put unrelated tasks in one tab set.
accessibility: Uses tablist and tab roles.
Production state should wire keyboard arrow navigation.
agentGuidance: Use Tabs for local view switching inside a page.
Use Sidebar or Menu for app-level navigation.

entries.name: Breadcrumb
entries.description: Breadcrumb shows the user's path through nested pages or workspace hierarchy.

props.name: items
props.description: Ordered path items with optional current state.

useWhen: Use on detail pages nested inside a broader workspace.
Use when users need a quick way back to parent contexts.
doNotUseWhen: Do not use breadcrumbs as the primary navigation.
Do not show breadcrumbs on shallow one-page tools.
accessibility: Uses a breadcrumb nav landmark.
The current page item sets aria-current.
agentGuidance: Use Breadcrumb above page titles for nested detail screens.
Keep labels short and page-like.

entries.name: Pagination
entries.description: Pagination moves through pages of tabular, list, or search-result content.
useWhen: Use for paged tables, source lists, and search results.
Keep the active page clearly visible.
doNotUseWhen: Do not use for short lists that fit comfortably on one page.
Do not hide previous and next labels behind icons only.
accessibility: Uses a pagination nav landmark.
The current page sets aria-current.
agentGuidance: Use Pagination when content is split into numbered pages.
Use infinite scroll only if specifically requested by product.

entries.name: Menu
entries.description: Menu presents a compact list of destinations or actions with icon and metadata slots.

props.name: items
props.description: Menu rows with label, meta, and active state.

useWhen: Use in popovers, drawers, or compact navigation panels.
Use metadata when choices need clarification.
doNotUseWhen: Do not use Menu for long data collections.
Do not put destructive actions beside routine navigation without separation.
accessibility: Uses menu and menuitem roles.
Production behavior should add roving focus and Escape handling.
agentGuidance: Use Menu for compact navigation or action groups.
Use Sidebar for persistent app navigation.

entries.name: Steps
entries.description: Steps show progress through a linear workflow such as setup, analysis, and publish.

props.name: items
props.description: Ordered steps with label, description, and status.

useWhen: Use for linear setup, review, approval, and publish flows.
Use concise labels and one-line descriptions.
doNotUseWhen: Do not use for non-linear navigation.
Do not show too many steps without grouping.
accessibility: Steps render as an ordered list.
Status is visible through text context and icon state.
agentGuidance: Use Steps when a user must understand where they are in a process.
Use Progress for percentage completion instead.

entries.name: Sidebar Nav Item
entries.description: Sidebar Nav Item is the repeatable row primitive for persistent workspace sidebars.
useWhen: Use inside Sidebar for route-level navigation.
Use badges for counts or status only when they help scanning.
doNotUseWhen: Do not use for command menus or one-off action lists.
Do not make labels icon-only in dense enterprise tools.
accessibility: The item is keyboard reachable and keeps visible text.
Use link semantics in production when routing.
agentGuidance: Use Sidebar Nav Item as the child primitive for app sidebars.
Use Menu Item patterns for popover menus.
entries.code:
import { SidebarNavItem } from "./SidebarNavItem";

<SidebarNavItem active label="Agent chat" meta="Conversation workspace" />

entries.name: Command Palette
entries.description: Command Palette lets users search pages, commands, sources, and agent workflows from one overlay.

props.name: commands
props.description: Command rows with label, description, and type.

useWhen: Use for cross-workspace search and fast command execution.
Use when the product has many agent workflows or pages.
doNotUseWhen: Do not use as the only way to access core navigation.
Do not include unsafe actions without confirmation.
accessibility: Search input has a label and results are buttons.
Production overlay should manage focus, Escape, and keyboard selection.
agentGuidance: Use Command Palette for global search and task launch.
Use Quick Action Panel when commands should stay visible on a dashboard.

entries.name: Badge / Pill
entries.description: Badges and pills label status, severity, filters, versions, and compact metadata.

props.name: dot
props.description: Adds a small status dot before the label.

useWhen: Use badges for compact status or metadata.
Use dot badges for presence or run state.
Use filter pills when values can be toggled.
doNotUseWhen: Do not use color alone to communicate status.
Do not use badges as primary actions.

Pair badges with tables, cards, and tool-call rows.

entries.name: Avatar
entries.description: Avatars identify people, agents, and presence states across chat, navigation, and lists.

props.name: shape
props.description: Controls whether the avatar represents a person or an AI agent.

props.name: initials
props.description: Fallback text when no image is provided.

useWhen: Use circular avatars for people.
Use rounded-square avatars for agents.
Use status dots only when presence matters.
doNotUseWhen: Do not infer personal identity from an image.
Do not use decorative avatars without an accessible label when identity matters.

Keep status paired with text nearby when status is important.
agentGuidance: Use agent shape for assistants and tools.
Use user shape for people in chat and navigation.

entries.name: Divider
entries.description: Dividers separate related content, toolbar groups, list sections, and panel regions.
useWhen: Use dividers to separate related groups.

doNotUseWhen: Do not use dividers to compensate for weak hierarchy.
Do not over-separate every small element.

Do not place focus on passive dividers.
agentGuidance: Use dividers inside cards, sidebars, tables, and topbars when grouping helps scanning.

entries.name: Tooltip
entries.description: Tooltips provide short contextual help for icons, metrics, and unfamiliar controls.
useWhen: Use tooltips to answer what an icon or metric means.
Keep tooltip copy short and specific.
doNotUseWhen: Do not hide required information only in a tooltip.
Do not use tooltips for long instructions.
accessibility: Tooltip appears on hover and focus-within.
Trigger controls still need accessible names.
agentGuidance: Use tooltips for compact explanatory text, not onboarding copy.
Prefer visible helper text for form requirements.

<Tooltip content="This explains the metric.">

</Tooltip>

entries.name: Surface / Card Base
entries.description: Surface is the base container primitive for cards, panels, selected regions, and repeated items.

Agent status

Ready to run

doNotUseWhen: Do not use for decorative clustering.
Do not hide critical ownership only in initials.
accessibility: Each visible avatar receives an accessible label.
Overflow count is visible text.
agentGuidance: Use Avatar Group when a row or card has multiple owners.
Use Avatar for one identity and Agent Avatar for AI-specific status.

entries.name: Analytics Agent Workspace
entries.description: A full agent workspace combining chat, tool activity, citations, source review, charts, and insight cards.
useWhen: Use as the reference composition for analytics chat surfaces.
Use when an agent answer needs evidence, dashboard context, and follow-up actions.
doNotUseWhen: Do not use this full template for a compact embedded assistant.
Do not remove source review when claims require evidence.
accessibility: Composed from semantic sections, buttons, and readable message order.
Future production shell should manage chat scroll and source drawer focus.
agentGuidance: Compose from Chat Surface, Chat Message, Citation Chip, Tool Call Card, Source Drawer, Summary Chart Card, and Insight Card.
Keep the chat stream and source review adjacent when an answer depends on evidence.

entries.name: Dashboard Overview
entries.description: A product dashboard shell with sidebar, topbar, workspace header, metrics, charts, activity, and quick actions.
useWhen: Use as the baseline for Nexus and cross-project dashboard pages.
Use when teams need a balanced view of metrics, work activity, and next actions.
doNotUseWhen: Do not use this density for marketing landing pages.
Do not add unrelated cards just to fill the grid.
accessibility: Uses visible labels across navigation, search, and card actions.
Chart panels need production text alternatives for underlying data.
agentGuidance: Compose with Topbar, Sidebar, Dashboard Header, Grid, Panel, Summary Chart Card, Activity Feed, and Quick Action Panel.
Use this template when generating operational dashboards, not conversational-first pages.

entries.name: INCI Lookup View
entries.description: A product-information workflow for ingredient lookup, file upload, source review, and evidence-backed summary.
useWhen: Use for product information, ingredient, and source-review workflows.
Use when the workflow starts with structured lookup fields and source evidence.
doNotUseWhen: Do not use for general dashboards where product lookup is not the primary task.
Do not show regulatory or ingredient claims without source context.
accessibility: Fields keep visible labels and source rows remain readable.
Production combobox and date behaviors should use full keyboard support.
agentGuidance: Compose with Panel, Form Field, Combobox, File Upload, Description List, Empty State, Source Drawer, and Badge.
Use this template when generating product intelligence or INCI workflows.

entries.name: Empty State Library
entries.description: A reusable set of empty-state blocks for conversation, source, and insight-first workflows.
useWhen: Use when a workspace has no content yet and the next best action is clear.
Use to keep blank pages useful and calm.
doNotUseWhen: Do not use vague empty-state copy.
Do not show more than one primary action per empty state.
accessibility: Each empty state has a visible title, description, and labeled action.
Icon meaning is supported by text.
agentGuidance: Use Empty State Library patterns for first-run, no-source, and no-insight states.
Make the action specific to the missing content.

entries.name: Marketing Workspace
entries.description: A marketing-agent workspace for campaign analysis, brief generation, audience direction, and chat follow-up.
useWhen: Use for campaign planning and agent-assisted brief generation.
Use when marketing teams need charts, structured inputs, and conversation in one workspace.
doNotUseWhen: Do not use for pure reporting dashboards without brief generation.
Do not publish agent suggestions without source or review context.
accessibility: Composed from labeled fields, sections, buttons, and readable chat order.
Production chart data should include non-visual summaries.
agentGuidance: Compose with Dashboard Header, Insight Card, Quick Action Panel, Panel, Form Field, Textarea, Chat Surface, and Suggestion Chips.
Use this template when the workflow output is a campaign brief or marketing recommendation.

entries.name: Auth Screen
entries.description: A restrained internal-tool sign-in screen with trust messaging, form fields, validation, and primary action.
useWhen: Use for internal product authentication and protected design-library contexts.
Use when permission and trust messaging must be clear.
doNotUseWhen: Do not use as a marketing landing page.
Do not add decorative content that distracts from sign-in.
accessibility: Fields have visible labels and the primary action has visible text.
Production auth should use real form semantics and identity-provider behavior.
agentGuidance: Compose with Alert, Form Field, Input, Validation Message, and Button.
Keep auth screens quiet, direct, and security-focused.

entries.name: Citation Review Block
entries.description: A review block for inspecting an agent answer, mapped citations, source drawer, and approval actions.
useWhen: Use when an agent answer needs human review before publishing.
Use when citations and source evidence must stay visible together.
doNotUseWhen: Do not use for answers without source evidence.
Do not hide approval context behind a modal if review is the main task.
accessibility: The answer and sources remain in readable order.
Approval actions use visible labels.
agentGuidance: Compose with Panel, Citation Chip, Source Drawer, Description List, Badge, and Button.
Use this block whenever a workflow needs citation-backed approval.

entries.name: Settings Form Screen
entries.description: A settings workflow for configuring workspace details, agent behavior, review dates, and save actions.
useWhen: Use for admin settings, workspace setup, and agent configuration pages.
Use when a form needs grouped sections and clear save/cancel behavior.
doNotUseWhen: Do not use for short inline edits where a modal or panel is enough.
Do not mix unrelated settings in one section.
accessibility: Fields and controls keep visible labels.
Validation appears near the actions and uses text plus icon.
agentGuidance: Compose with Alert, Form Section, Form Group, Form Field, Combobox, Date Picker, Switch, Checkbox, Validation Message, and Form Actions.
Use this template when generating configuration or setup workflows.
